Items.Title: A Psalm for the Wild-Built (Becky Chambers)
Items.Flavor: A tea monk and a robot walk into the wilderness to ask what people need. You read it slowly, on purpose.

Items.Title: Station Eleven (Emily St. John Mandel)
Items.Flavor: A travelling theatre troupe after the end of everything. It used to read like a warning. Now it reads like a letter from a friend.

Items.Title: The Left Hand of Darkness (Ursula K. Le Guin)
Items.Flavor: A long walk across the ice beside someone you don't understand yet. By the end, you do.

Items.Title: Middlemarch (George Eliot)
Items.Flavor: Eight hundred pages of ordinary lives in a small town. The ordinary lives turn out to be the whole point.

Items.Title: The Remains of the Day (Kazuo Ishiguro)
Items.Flavor: A butler drives through the countryside, almost saying what he means, mile after mile.

Items.Title: Music for Airports (Brian Eno)
Items.Flavor: Built to make waiting rooms bearable. It works on orbiters too.

Items.Title: Kind of Blue (Miles Davis)
Items.Flavor: Unhurried and cool, like the musicians had all the time in the world. Maybe they did.

Items.Title: Blue (Joni Mitchell)
Items.Flavor: Just a voice, a dulcimer, and nothing held back.

Items.Title: In Rainbows (Radiohead)
Items.Flavor: Warm and restless at once. Best heard with the lights low.

Items.Title: Pet Sounds (The Beach Boys)
Items.Flavor: Sunlit harmonies with something aching underneath.

Items.Title: The Disintegration Loops (William Basinski)
Items.Flavor: Old tape loops slowly crumbling as they play. Beautiful in a way that's hard to explain up here.

Items.Title: Carrie & Lowell (Sufjan Stevens)
Items.Flavor: Quiet songs about grief, sung barely above a whisper.

Items.Title: Selected Ambient Works 85-92 (Aphex Twin)
Items.Flavor: Machines dreaming in soft focus. Fitting company.

Items.Title: Vespertine (Bjork)
Items.Flavor: Music boxes, whispers and snowfall. It sounds like being indoors on a winter night.

Items.Title: Moon Safari (Air)
Items.Flavor: Lounge-y and starry-eyed. Someone imagined space would feel like this, and sometimes it does.

Items.Title: WALL-E
Items.Flavor: A small robot tidies a dead Earth and falls in love. You try not to take it personally.

Items.Title: My Neighbor Totoro
Items.Flavor: Two sisters, a new house, and a forest spirit at the bus stop in the rain. Nothing bad happens. That's the gift.

Items.Title: Paddington 2
Items.Flavor: If we're kind and polite, the world will be right. Hard to argue with.

Items.Title: Spirited Away
Items.Flavor: A girl works in a bathhouse for spirits and doesn't forget her own name.

Items.Title: The Iron Giant
Items.Flavor: A giant machine decides what kind of machine it wants to be.

Items.Title: Arrival
Items.Flavor: Learning a language that changes how you see time. You'd make the same choice, too.

Items.Title: Paris, Texas
Items.Flavor: A man walks out of the desert and slowly finds his way back to people.

Items.Title: Stalker
Items.Flavor: Three men cross a forbidden Zone toward a room that grants wishes. Long, quiet, and green.

Items.Title: Tampopo
Items.Flavor: A truck driver helps a widow perfect her ramen. Mostly it's a love letter to eating.

Items.Title: Moonstruck
Items.Flavor: Brooklyn, opera, a full moon, and a family too loud to be unhappy for long.

Contacts.Name: Mara
Contacts.Situation: Tending a rooftop garden above the waterline. She waves your bot over and asks, mostly, whether the stars still look the same from up there.

Locations.Name: Flooded Suburb
Locations.Flavor: Rows of houses stand knee-deep in still, brown water. Mailboxes break the surface like grave markers. Something moves behind a curtain that hasn't been drawn in years.

Locations.Name: Overgrown Transit Hub
Locations.Flavor: A train station swallowed by green. Vines climb the departure boards; a tree has grown straight up through platform four. Birdsong, of all things. Actual birdsong.
